title: Unicode escape resume policy and truncation mitigation for streamed structured JSON
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Edge-case resilience for streamed JSON outputs where partial token boundaries, multi-byte Unicode escapes (\uXXXX), and interleaved tool/function call markers cause truncation or invalid payloads. This ticket defines a deterministic resume policy, an escape/unescape normalization step, and lightweight repair heuristics to maximize successful ingestion by clients while maintaining idempotent retries for tool-calls.
background: We often receive truncated streamed payloads from models in hosted and dedicated modes. Truncation near multi-byte Unicode sequences (e.g., broken surrogate pairs or half-escaped sequences) and split escape tokens break downstream JSON parsers and tool-call handshakes. Existing heuristics (artifact in ENG-8342) handle many cases but leave rare Unicode boundary failures and tool-call idempotency gaps. Customers report errors during tool handoffs and SDK teams maintain multiple ad-hoc client-side patches.
proposed_solution: 1) Attach a compact resume-token manifest to each stream chunk header: (cursor-id, byte-offset, 16-bit checksum). 2) On truncation detection, runtime emits a 'resume' event containing the last well-formed object index and resume-token. 3) Implement server-side escape normalization pass that converts broken or split Unicode escape fragments into safe U+FFFD placeholders when repairable within a small lookback window. 4) For tool/function calls include an idempotency token in the call envelope and persist call receipts on the server for 60s to dedupe retries. 5) Expose a backward-compatible compatibility flag (compat.unicode-resume=v1) so older clients ignore resume events.
tradeoffs:
- Repairing escapes can hide model bugs; we will only substitute placeholders when checksum and heuristic window indicate high confidence.
- Persisting receipts increases memory pressure under heavy short-lived bursts; we limit retention to 60s and store compact receipts only for requests flagged as tool-calls.
- Adding resume metadata increases header size slightly; we will use a compact binary encoding and base64 for REST fallbacks.
milestone: Design signoff (2025-11-18), Runtime prototype (2025-11-26), SDK adapters (2025-12-03), Canary rollout (2025-12-10)
acceptance_criteria:
1) Streams with truncated UTF-8/Unicode escapes must be repairable by server with placeholders in >= 95% synthetic cases; validated by fuzz tests.
2) Tool/function calls resumed after a truncation must not trigger duplicate side-effects when idempotency token is present.
3) Resume-token header accepted by JS/Go/Python SDKs and falls back safely for unsupported clients.
4) Latency regression < 1% p50 for normal non-truncated requests.
5) Documentation and migration guide published in Confluence.
implementation_notes:
- Implement compact resume token generation in runtime stream encoder.
- Add escape normalization pass as an optional stage before framing.
- Add small in-memory receipt store keyed by (customer, idempotency-token) with TTL.
- Update streaming envelope spec and add compatibility flag.
- Add unit + integration tests: fuzz Unicode, simulate abrupt connection cut, verify resume & dedupe.
- Coordinate with SDK owners for adapters.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for escape-normalizer covering: split \u escapes, surrogate halves, multi-byte UTF-8 fragmentation.
- Fuzz harness with 100k truncated inputs and assert parser success or controlled placeholder insertion.
- Integration test that simulates network cut after N bytes and uses resume token to request continuation; assert JSON validity and tool-call idempotency.
- Load test to confirm memory impact of receipt store under bursty traffic.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-gate behind runtime flag (off by default). 2) Enable in internal staging and run regression suite. 3) Canary on 5% of hosted traffic with metric dashboards (invalid-json-rate, toolcall-duplicate-rate, p50 latency). 4) Gradually increase to 50% then 100% after 2 weeks with no regression.
